newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields down, off lows, crown firms.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields down, off lows, crown firms.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were lower on Friday morning, despite coming off early lows, and the crown was firmer.
The market kept riding on the Riksbank's latest quarterly inflation report, presented on Thursday, and stronger foreign markets, but both yields and the crown seemed to stabilising, dealers said.
"We have seen some profit taking at the same time as German yields are still going strong and the crown is firmer," a trader said.
Players were relieved after Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's speech did not affect U.S. yields to a wider extent.
The six-month T-bill rate fell four basis points to 4.20 percent and the ten-year bond yield dropped six to 7.34.
The crown firmed to 4.5220 crowns against the mark from 4.5370 late on Thursday.

"There are still tendencies to crown buying, but it has calmed down and stabilised after Thursday's strong demand," a trader said. Foreigners and Swedish export companies were, however, buying crowns, dealers said.
